quick_skim.title: DIGS: Distribution-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation
quick_skim.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian segmentation typically binds semantic features to the per-Gaussian state via per-scene gradient training (1-4 h) or the more recent closed-form distillation. Both commit each primitive to a single feature; therefore, boundary Gaussians spanning multiple 2D instances are forced into a hard decision that degrades retrieval accuracy and yields unstable mask boundaries at render time. We present DIGS, a training-free framework with two stages, class-agnostic mapping and multi-modal encoding, that decouples instance discovery from linguistic naming. At the Gaussian level, our distribution-informed representation maintains an explicit top-$M$ label distribution per primitive, updated by a tempered Dirichlet rule; preservation of multi-peaked label distributions at boundary primitives allows a late-argmax renderer to recover clean instance boundaries. A bidirectional state machine aggregates these distributions into a persistent class-agnostic instance ontology. The instance-level encoding stage then fuses the CLIP visual embedding of each instance's isolated 3D footprint with the CLIP-text embedding of an LLM-generated attribute description, disambiguating visually similar instances. On a single A100, DIGS completes mapping and instance encoding on LERF-OVS in 1.0-3.2 min per scene, depending on whether LLM fusion is enabled, and serves native 3D queries in 5.4 ms. It reaches 71.95% mean mIoU on LERF-OVS, outperforming both the training-free SFS and training-based LaGa baselines. DIGS also achieves the highest mean mIoU on LERF-Mask and 3D-OVS and surpasses Gaga and ObjectGS on Replica under their respective evaluation protocols. Code is available at https://github.com/ZephyrZos/DIGS.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian segmentation usually hard-assigns each primitive one feature, blurring boundaries. DIGS is training-free, decoupling instance discovery from naming via per-primitive top-M label distributions.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 开放词汇三维高斯分割通常将每个高斯基元绑定到单一语义特征，跨实例的边界基元被迫硬决策，导致检索精度下降与渲染时掩码边界不稳定。作者提出免训练框架 DIGS，先做类无关的实例映射再做多模态编码，并用逐基元的 Top-M 标签分布表示语义。实验表明该分布化表示提升了检索精度与边界稳定性，将实例发现与语言命名解耦。
